question: What is vendor-managed inventory?
html:
Vendor-managed inventory (VMI) means we manage a customer's supply stock for them. We track what their lab uses, decide when to reorder, and keep shelves filled, so their staff don't have to place routine orders. Our growth plan names VMI as a way to make accounts stickier (Thomas Scientific growth plan).

How it works

  • We agree with the lab on a list of consumables and target stock levels.
  • We monitor usage at the site.
  • We replenish before items run short, based on that usage.
  • Terms such as ownership of stock and billing timing are set in each customer agreement.
Customer-orderedVendor-managed
Who watches stockLab staffThomas Scientific
Who triggers reordersLab staffThomas Scientific
Switching effort for the labLowHigher, est.

Where it fits our plan

  • VMI sits in our thesis next to punchout ordering, private label and specialty verticals (Thomas Scientific growth plan).
  • The plan says margin has to come from mix. VMI's role is retention: it makes accounts sticky (Thomas Scientific growth plan).
  • The candidate pool is our scored demand map. It covers 27,503 lab, pathology and hospital sites, with 713 rated Pursue and 2,317 Nurture (Thomas Scientific growth plan).
  • The plan's AI agents for forecasting could support replenishment decisions. This link is inferred, not stated (est.).

What we don't know yet

The context has no VMI figures. To size the opportunity we would need:

  • the current list of VMI accounts and their revenue,
  • gross margin and cost to serve per VMI account, including on-site labor,
  • retention and renewal rates for VMI accounts versus customer-ordered accounts,
  • the inventory we hold for VMI customers.

Constraint on timing

  • The first-lien loan was marked at 88.3% of par in Jun 2026 and matures Dec 14, 2027. The plan sequences every lever behind liquidity and refinancing (Thomas Scientific growth plan).
  • VMI may require us to hold more stock for customers. That would use working capital while cash is the priority (est.).

Sticky, recurring accounts are part of the evidence lenders and buyers need to value Thomas above a commodity distributor before the Dec 14, 2027 maturity.

Next actions

  1. Pull a list of current VMI accounts with revenue, margin and retention, and compare them with customer-ordered accounts.
  2. Estimate the working capital VMI would require per account before offering it more widely.
  3. Flag which Pursue and Nurture sites have usage patterns that suit VMI.
  4. Add VMI retention to the account-health metrics the AI agents are planned to track.
